Each link opens that job's log. This issue stays open while the run is red and the next run that passes every job closes it. `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <branch>` runs it again on demand.

Night bot: this run is on `main`, so it is yours, and it comes first (`priority:high`): production promotes itself only from a run on `main` that passes every job, so it waits on this fix. Root-cause each failed job from its log and fix it in a pull request: a flake is not a root cause, so make a flaky test robust instead of re-running it, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green. Reproduce it with the job's own command (CLAUDE.md, Commands; one fuzz seed is `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1`, with `--handicap` for the handicapped wave and `--duos` for the Duos wave; a daily test is `cargo test -p <crate> <name> -- --ignored`). A pull request's CI runs only the e2e smoke specs and leaves the tests marked `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` out, so say in the pull request which job here the fix makes pass and how you checked it. _Posted by `.github/workflows/super.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-8` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41775558934)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Make super run job `e2e component (chrome)` pass again on `main`: `pnpm --dir e2e exec cypress run --component --browser chrome`. I could not read the failed run's log, so I reproduced the job locally and found the root cause of each failure. The Chrome pin from #2969 was not the cause: Chrome 156 here, 691 of 699 tests green, and 8 red. Four causes remain, and each gets a fix that keeps its assertion (no skip, no retry, no raised timeout):

1. `mobile-ux.cy.tsx`, "B31 at 390x844 the board is at most 820 px tall" reads 832.
2. `practice-table.cy.tsx`, "#2878 mid-game: no HUD above the board" at landscape 844x390: the hero starts 41px below the content top, and the spec allows 24.
3. `practice-table.cy.tsx`, "#2878 game over: one outcome, in the board's chip", all six viewports: it counts 3 visible outcome words and expects 1.
4. The same game-over test at phone 390x844 and 390x664 hits a real overlap once cause 3 is out of the way: the chip covers the control bar.

## Root causes (measured)

1. #2917 (`b2217c07d`) made `.game > .turn-banner` out of flow, so the board now fills the viewport less the shell's 12px vertical padding: 844 − 12 = 832. The bound 820 dates from Polish 7 (`bb59a4913`), when the banner pill took height. The landscape B31 test already says "B46's vertical shell padding leaves 378px" (390 − 12). The spec is stale and the product is fine.
2. `board.css` has `@media (orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 500px)`: "Each seat fills its side's half of the field's height, with the hero and piles in its middle" (`align-content: center`). By design the hero is not at the top there; the seat plate is (4px from the content top). The spec is wrong for that layout only.
3. `OUTCOME_WORDS` (`/\b(win|loss|victory|defeat|draw)\b/i`) matches the board's modifier badge `button.modifier-badge`, text `Your cards gain "Combo: draw 1"`, from `fullBoardView()` in `apps/web/src/test/fixtures.ts`. Rule text is not an outcome. The badges live in `[data-testid^="modifiers-"]`; the spec already uses `modifiers-you` and `modifiers-opponent`.
4. This is a real UI defect that cause 3 hid. The practice route's "won't earn" notice (`.practice-unearned`, about 70px with its padding) sits inside `.board-notices` in the control bar. At game over the chip is in flow under the board (about 64px). At 390 wide the board's content overflows its box: scrollHeight 812 against 766 at 844 tall, and the cards are already at their 44px floor at 664 tall. The control bar then spills over the chip, and the screenshot shows the chip over End turn, log and the gear.
   - Hiding the notice at every width is not enough. At tablet 768x1024 a latent overflow appears: the revealed opponent hand (R434) makes the board content 1010 against 946. Today the notice only masks that, by pushing the buttons below the chip. That is why the hide rule below must stay inside the `max-width: 600px` media query.

I validated all four fixes on untracked scratch copies of the two specs, since deleted. The `mobile-ux` copy passed 87 of 87 and the `practice-table` copy 38 of 38, with the CSS rule injected through a `<style>` element.

## Files to touch

| File | New/change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e/cypress/component/mobile-ux.cy.tsx` | change | B31 portrait test: bound 820 becomes 832, title follows, with a one-line comment |
| `e2e/cypress/component/practice-table.cy.tsx` | change | Add constants `LANDSCAPE_PHONE_QUERY` and `ENEMY_TOP_MAX_PX`; the hero assertion measures the opponent seat at the landscape-phone query; the outcome-word scan skips modifier badges |
| `apps/web/src/practice/practice.css` | change | One new rule inside `@media (max-width: 600px)`: hide the unearned notice's strip once the board has folded to its chip |

Do not touch:
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/` and `.claude/`.
- `e2e/cypress.config.ts` and `e2e/support/chrome-pin.ts` (the pin stays as #2969 left it).
- `apps/web/src/game/board.css` and `animations.css`.
- `apps/web/src/routes/practice.tsx`: `practice.test.tsx` R1303000 expects the notice in the DOM at game over, so hide it with CSS only.
- Any crate.
- `retries` or timeouts.

No spec section or ruling governs this (test and layout repair, no rules decision), so add no `R<n>` note. Cite no new `R`-id in the comments, because `cargo jackioh spec check` cross-checks them.

## Steps

0. Setup. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` has normally run already. Check that `apps/web/src/wasm/pkg/jackioh_wasm_bg.wasm` exists; if not, run `JACKIOH_WASM_LUAU=0 sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` (about 4 minutes with the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`). Check that `~/.cache/Cypress/16.1.0` exists. If it does not, unset `CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY` and run `pnpm --dir e2e exec cypress install`. `Xvfb` is on the runner. Always run Cypress with `CI=true`.

1. `e2e/cypress/component/mobile-ux.cy.tsx`, the `it("B31 at 390x844 …")` test (about line 517). Replace it with:
   ```ts
   it("B31 at 390x844 the board is at most 832 px tall and the log is hidden", () => {
     cy.viewport(390, 844);
     mountGame(fullBoardView());

     cy.get(BOARD).should(($board) => {
       // Nothing is drawn above the board (#2917), so B46's vertical shell padding leaves 832px of 844 for it.
       expect(rectOf($board[0] as Element).height).to.be.at.most(832);
     });
     cy.get(ts("log")).should("not.be.visible");
   });
   ```
   Keep the `cy.get(ts("log"))` line and the closing as they are today.

2. `e2e/cypress/component/practice-table.cy.tsx`, constants. Directly above `/** The outcome words the one visible outcome may wear. */` (line 42) add:
   ```ts
   /** board.css's phone-on-its-side layout. */
   const LANDSCAPE_PHONE_QUERY = "(orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 500px)";

   /** How far below the shell's content top the enemy's topmost plate may start. */
   const ENEMY_TOP_MAX_PX = 24;
   ```

3. Same file, the hero assertion in "#2878 mid-game: no HUD above the board" (the block from the comment at about line 282 to its `.to.be.at.most(24);`). Replace it with:
   ```ts
   // The opponent's hero starts right under the shell's safe-area padding. On a phone held on its side
   // board.css centers each hero and its piles in their seat's half of the field's height, so there the
   // seat's plate is what starts at the top.
   const hero = doc.querySelector('[data-testid="hero-opponent"]');
   expect(hero, "hero-opponent is mounted").to.not.eq(null);
   const seat = doc.querySelector(".seat-opponent");
   expect(seat, "the opponent's seat is mounted").to.not.eq(null);
   const win = doc.defaultView;
   if (hero === null || seat === null || win === null) return;
   const topmost = win.matchMedia(LANDSCAPE_PHONE_QUERY).matches ? seat : hero;
   expect(
     topmost.getBoundingClientRect().top - contentTop,
     `${topmost === seat ? "the opponent's seat" : "hero-opponent"} starts within ${String(ENEMY_TOP_MAX_PX)}px of the shell's content top at ${where}`,
   ).to.be.at.most(ENEMY_TOP_MAX_PX);
   ```

4. Same file, the outcome-word scan in "#2878 game over: one outcome, in the board's chip" (about line 409). Directly after `if (child.closest("[hidden]") !== null) return;` and before `const text = child.textContent ?? "";`, add:
   ```ts
   // A modifier badge's rule text ("Combo: draw 1") is not an outcome.
   if (child.closest('[data-testid^="modifiers-"]') !== null) return;
   ```

5. `apps/web/src/practice/practice.css`. Insert the block below right after the `.practice-table .practice-unearned button { … }` rule and before `@media (max-width: 600px), (orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 500px)` (about line 1674):
   ```css
   /* Once the game is over the board folds to its chip, which stands in flow under it (animations.css).
      A phone has no height for the "won't earn" row above the controls as well: at 390x844 the board's
      content spilled 46px over the chip, and at 390x664 the cards were already at their 44px floor, so the
      control bar sat under the chip. The result dialog the chip's Result button reopens carries the same
      line (practice-result-earning), so the board's own copy steps aside. Phones held upright only: a
      tablet and a phone on its side fit with it. */
   @media (max-width: 600px) {
     .practice-table > .game:has(> [data-testid="result-overlay"][data-form="chip"]) .board-notices:has(> .practice-unearned) {
       display: none;
     }
   }
   ```
   Keep the `@media (max-width: 600px)` wrapper. No numbers beyond the existing 600px, and no colours or font sizes, so `typescale.test.ts`, `palette.test.ts` and `cursors.test.ts` are unaffected.

## Tests

The specs are the tests. Without the CSS rule (step 5), the game-over test is red at 390x844 and 390x664. Without step 4 it is red at all six viewports.

- `cd e2e && CI=true E2E_COMPONENT_PORT=5281 pnpm exec cypress run --component --browser chrome --spec cypress/component/practice-table.cy.tsx` expects 38 passing (about 40 s).
- `cd e2e && CI=true E2E_COMPONENT_PORT=5282 pnpm exec cypress run --component --browser chrome --spec cypress/component/mobile-ux.cy.tsx` expects 87 passing (about 30 s).
- The job's own command, from the repo root: `CI=true pnpm --dir e2e exec cypress run --component --browser chrome`. Expect "All specs passed!", 35 of 35 specs, 699 tests (about 7 minutes). Pull-request CI never runs component specs, so this run is the proof; say in the pull request that the fix makes `e2e component (chrome)` pass and quote this result.
- `pnpm exec eslint e2e/cypress/component/practice-table.cy.tsx e2e/cypress/component/mobile-ux.cy.tsx`.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/practice.test.tsx src/practice` (the notice stays in the DOM, so these must still pass).
- `pnpm --dir e2e typecheck:component` fails only in `apps/web/src/wasm/luau.ts` ("Cannot find module './pkg/luau/…'") when the Luau module was not built; that is not caused by this change. Any other error is.

## Done when

- [ ] `mobile-ux.cy.tsx` B31 passes at 832.
- [ ] Both `practice-table.cy.tsx` failures are fixed: the landscape hero check and the six game-over viewports.
- [ ] The full local component run is green on Chrome 156 (35/35 specs).
- [ ] eslint is clean on the two specs, and the two web unit paths above pass.
- [ ] Checks from the harness list: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests and web tests. No Rust or catalog change, so they are untouched; `git status --porcelain -- apps/web/src/wire` stays empty.
- [ ] `git status` shows only the three files in the table.
- [ ] No skip, `.only`, `eslint-disable`, retry, raised timeout or lowered threshold.
- [ ] The pull request says: job `e2e component (chrome)`; the four root causes; how it was checked (the commands and counts above); the latent tablet issue; and that Chrome 154, the pinned Chrome on CI when the runner's Chrome is 155, could not be run locally.

## Risks

- I verified on Chrome 156. CI may run Chrome 155 (pinned to 154 by `pinChrome`). Only layout measurements changed here, not pixel samples, so the risk is low. If a pixel spec (`card-versions`, `full-art-finishes`, `animated-art`) is red on CI, that is a new, separate failure; the plan has no evidence of one.
- The CSS rule is phone-portrait only. Tablet 768x1024 has a latent game-over overflow that the notice masks: the revealed opponent hand (R434) makes the board content about 64px taller than the board. Do not widen or drop the media query (it turns that viewport red), and do not "fix" tablet in this change. Report it in the pull request as a follow-up for a person to file; the bot cannot create issues from here.
- Cypress `should` callbacks must not call commands (`cy.task` and the like). My edits add none.
- Edit the test names only as written (B31). Nothing else cites them: `rg "at most 820"` finds only this spec.

## Open questions

None that block the build. For a person, later: the 768x1024 revealed-hand overflow above, and whether practice should stop showing the "won't earn" notice at game over on every width (a product call that would also change `practice.test.tsx` R1303000).
